title: Gone Fishing
teaser: The classic children's card game by a quiet pond. Ask your rivals for cards, remember what they asked for, and when someone says 'Go Fish!', cast your line and see what bites. Four of a kind becomes a fish in your bucket.

manPage.synopsis: gone fishing — ask your rivals for ranks you hold, cast for a card when told “Go Fish!”, and turn every book into a fish.
manPage.description: Muffy Barkocy wrote Go Fish for Berkeley's machines, with a computer of two minds: one that asks for its ranks in turn, and one that remembers what you asked for and asks it back. Its manual's only bug says the computer cheats only rarely, and it does: one time in a thousand-odd it peeks. Gone Fishing plays its rules exactly in Classic 1993 and adds a pond, three animal rivals with different memories, a notebook, a tournament and a fish for every book.

howToPlay: Ask one rival for a rank you hold. If they have any, they hand them all over and you ask again.
If not, they say “Go Fish!”: cast for a card. Catch the rank you asked for and you ask again.
Four of a rank make a book, and every book leaps into your bucket as a fish. Most books wins.
